fixes.explanation: Job 38:1 says the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind. After all those chapters of waiting for a reply, it arrives in the middle of a storm wind. I think Job stops talking and listens.

A pillar of cloud is what went before Israel by day in the wilderness (Exodus 13:21). It's a good guess, since a cloud and a wind are cousins. But Job 38:1 says the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind. Different way of showing up, and for Job the text says whirlwind.

Right on the money, baker. The LORD says, “I will question you, and you shall inform Me.” The roles flip. Job had said he wanted to speak to the Almighty and argue his case with God (Job 13:3), and now the LORD is the One asking, and Job is the one who has to answer.

Job 38:7 says the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy. Weeping is a fine thing in other places, but this verse names shouting for joy. When a cornerstone goes down, the sons of God shout.

The LORD says He fixed the sea's boundaries and set in place its bars and doors (Job 38:10). The sea bursts out, and it gets a limit. Bars and doors are things you put on a space to keep something where it belongs. It's like putting a fence around a very big, very loud dog.

Yes, the LORD speaks right to the sea. He declares, “You may come this far, but no farther…” (Job 38:11). Then He tells the proud waves they must stop. Most of us can't get a shopping cart to stop where we want, and here's the whole sea with a limit.
The LORD asks, “Have you journeyed to the vents of the sea…” (Job 38:16). It's a question about a trip down to the deep places of the sea. I once thought the back of a drawer was far down.
The Jordan isn't named anywhere in these verses. The LORD asks about the vents of the sea and the trenches of the deep (Job 38:16). That's the sea and the deep, not the Jordan.

That's what He asks. “Have the gates of death been revealed to you?” (Job 38:17). The next question asks it again with the shadow of death. This is a heavy place to go, so I'll just say it plainly: the LORD is asking whether Job has seen these gates.

Yes, friend. The LORD says He brings rain on a barren land, on a desert where no man lives (Job 38:26). Then He says it makes the parched wasteland sprout with tender grass (Job 38:27). The rain falls on a desert where no man lives.

That's the question that stands out. “Who has put wisdom in the heart or given understanding to the mind?” (Job 38:36). It comes right in the middle of the clouds and lightning. All that knowing the LORD keeps asking Job about had to come from somewhere.

That's in the Bible, but not here. Adam, the first man, gave names to the livestock, the birds of the air and every beast of the field (Genesis 2:20). In Job 38:36 the LORD asks who has put wisdom in the heart or given understanding to the mind. Different question, same LORD.

The Bible does tell us about a city builder. Cain, Adam's son, built a city (Genesis 4:17). But in Job 38:36 the LORD asks who has put wisdom in the heart or given understanding to the mind. No bricks in that question.
